61.0.0.en: 1 The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the poor; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; 2 To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; 3 To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.

61.0.1.en: Through the words of the prophet Isaiah, the Lord Christ presents to us a living program of His saving work, which He sets forth briefly yet with depth. It is this: 1. Humanity's enjoyment of the Holy Spirit, who renews human nature and enriches it, removes its corruption and grants it the new life that is in Christ Jesus, so that it delights in fellowship in the divine life... This gift was offered to us in the person of the Lord Christ, who says: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me” [1]. As we said before in the interpretation of the eleventh chapter, the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of the Son, not a stranger to Christ; but through the Incarnation He received His descent upon Him in the name of the Church and on behalf of those who believe in Him:

61.0.2.en: * The Holy Spirit departed from man because He could not dwell in corruption; but now a new man has appeared among mankind, and he alone makes the return of the Spirit possible, for this man is without sin.

61.0.3.en: * God promised to give the Spirit a second time to mankind... and there was no other way by which this grace could be restored to humanity without departing again, except in Jesus Christ... It is an eternal return, caused by a state of stability and steadfastness.

61.0.4.en: * Christ gave the Holy Spirit to His humanity, and thereby made the Spirit become familiar once more with our nature.

61.0.5.en: * The return of the Holy Spirit to man in Christ, God incarnate, the second Adam, is an eternal return. For the Holy Spirit descended upon the second Adam because of His righteousness. And righteousness in Christ is steadfast righteousness, because the union of divinity with humanity in the person of Christ is steadfast... and this is a sure guarantee for humanity and its stability in the new life.

61.0.6.en: St. Cyril the Great * The name “Christ” implies the One who anoints, the One who is anointed, and the anointing itself. The Father is the One who anoints, the Son is anointed, and the Spirit is the anointing.

61.0.7.en: St. Irenaeus * The Holy Spirit shone in the fullness of His being upon Him, for like rests upon like. As for you, after you came up from the font of holy water, the anointing was given to you, which is a symbol of that with which Christ was anointed; this is the Holy Spirit.

61.1.0.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem When the book of Isaiah was handed to the Lord Christ, He read this passage, “and he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down... And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears” (Lk 4:17-21). 2. The Lord Christ came to gladden the hearts of the poor with the gospel of His salvation, to bind up the brokenhearted and to grant freedom to the captives... counting His coming a true jubilee year, acceptable to the Lord and granting comfort to those who mourn (Isa 61:2; Lev 25:9, 40). 3. His coming is “the day of vengeance of our God” [2], in which He shattered the authority of the powers of darkness, the devil and his angels and his evil works. 4. The Lord establishes the believers as trees of righteousness, or the planting of the Lord in the divine Paradise [3], bearing beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that is, He pours out upon us His beauty, His joy and His praise in place of humiliation, mourning and despair!

61.2.s.en: 2. The new life of the Church:

61.2.0.en: 4 And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations. 5 And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers. 6 But ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves.

61.2.1.en: The mission of the Lord Christ, whom the Father anointed to preach good tidings to the poor, is “to repair the waste cities” that have become desolate through the generations. In every generation human nature has become like waste cities, needing to be torn down and rebuilt. This is the work of God the Creator, who establishes His Kingdom within us, and by His Holy Spirit transforms us from a dwelling of sin and evil into a sanctuary for the Lord. As for the strangers who feed our flocks, and the sons of the alien who keep watch over our land and work as vinedressers in our garden, they are the inner faculties of the soul and its impulses, which had become as though foreign and alien to the Lord and His Kingdom. They are brought into subjection anew, so that they are no longer a stumbling block in the way of our salvation but, on the contrary, a help to the soul, supporting it in its striving. This is as the Hebrew people did of old, when they carried gold, silver and fine garments out of Egypt and used them in setting up the tabernacle of meeting, instead of using them in the worship of idols in Egypt.

61.3.0.en: He says: “Ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD” [6], because when we put on the new nature through Baptism we become priests spiritually, lifting up our hands in prayer and offering our bodies as a sacrifice of love acceptable to the Father. St. Jerome calls this priesthood “the lay priesthood (Laic Priesthood).”

61.4.s.en: 3. The glorious life of the Church:

61.4.0.en: 7 For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them. 8 “For I the LORD love judgment, I hate him who seizes by wrong. And I will make their reward faithful, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them. 9 And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed.”

61.4.1.en: God grants His Church an abundance of inner glory, heavenly consolations and perpetual joy.

61.4.2.en: a. A double reward in place of the old afflictions: “For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double” [7].

61.4.3.en: What is the double reward that we enjoy in place of our shame? It is the enjoyment of the forgiveness of our sins and the attainment of the righteousness of Christ; in other words, the removal of the shame of sin and the enjoyment of the glory of Christ in us; pardon for us as rebellious slaves and our acceptance as children of God in Jesus Christ, the Only-Begotten Son.

61.4.4.en: The atoning work of Christ did not stop at paying the debt that weighed us down, but He gave us His righteousness that we might share His glory. The Apostle says: “For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory” (Col 3:3-4).

61.4.5.en: Perhaps by the double inheritance He also means the two resurrections: the first resurrection, which we receive here in our temporal life as we enjoy the risen life, and the second resurrection, when the Lord of glory comes on the clouds, that we may rise with Him and be found with Him in glory. As St. Augustine says: [We who have died a twofold death (the death of the soul and of the body) rise with a twofold resurrection. Until now we have risen one resurrection, which is the resurrection from sin, for we were buried with Him in Baptism, and we rose with Him through Baptism in the resurrection. This resurrection is salvation from our sins; the other resurrection is the resurrection of the body. He has given us the greater resurrection, and behold, we await the lesser! The first resurrection is greater than the second, for our salvation from our sins is greater than the resurrection of the body.]

61.4.6.en: If the mark of the kingdom of the devil is the selfishness that brings hatred, then the shame into which we fell is that we were marked by deadly selfishness. In place of this shame we have received the double inheritance, that is, love in its two complementary aspects, love of God and love of neighbor. It is as though the work of Christ in us is to shatter the ego, in order to give us a surpassing love for God and for His creation.

61.4.7.en: b. “Everlasting joy shall be unto them” [7]; since the life of the Church here is a pledge of the heavenly life, it is marked by a double glory in place of shame, and by love in place of selfishness... and so it bears the nature of joy and gladness! The secret of our joy is that we bear our Christ within us, that He may establish His joyful heavenly Kingdom in our depths.

61.5.0.en: c. “And I will make an everlasting covenant with them” [8]... The book of Isaiah often repeats the discussion of this covenant between God and His Church, declared in the body of the crucified Christ as the mystery of an eternal reconciliation.

61.6.0.en: d. A blessing in their spiritual fruits as in their seed: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed” [9]...

61.6.1.en: What is this blessed seed that the Gentiles recognize?

61.6.2.en: He does not mean our children according to the flesh, but rather those who become disciples of the Lord through us, who come to know salvation and receive the new birth through our living witness to the gospel of our salvation.

61.6.3.en: Perhaps by the seed and the offspring He meant the holy works that are the fruits of the Spirit of the Holy God in us, and the gift of His free grace in our life.

61.7.0.en: 10 I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with a turban, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels. 11 For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.

61.7.1.en: The true life of the Church is a life of perpetual wedding, filled with joy and gladness without interruption, in which we put on the garment of salvation as the garment of the eternal wedding, or as a general priestly garment...

61.7.2.en: “I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with a turban (crown), and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels” [10].

61.7.3.en: In some traditional churches the priest repeats the preceding verse when he puts on the priestly vestments to take part in the Liturgy of the Eucharist, regarding himself as approaching the sacrament of the Eucharist as one approaches a joyful wedding, needing to put on the invisible garments of salvation, the robe of righteousness and the adornment of the Spirit... What is this garment but the Lord Christ Himself?! The believers put Him on when they enjoy the waters of Baptism (Gal 3:27).

61.7.4.en: * Truly Christ is the adornment of the bride, He who is, and who was, and who is to come, blessed now and forever, Amen.

61.7.5.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * Now (after Baptism), since you have taken off your old garments and put on the white garments spiritually, it is fitting for you to continue wearing what is white. Of course we do not mean by this that you should wear a white garment at all times, but that you should wrap yourselves in white garments in truth, shining spiritually, and say with the blessed Isaiah: “My soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation...”.

61.7.6.en: * Keep the holy day, clothed in the garment of salvation, Jesus Christ.

61.8.0.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem The prophet explained what he means by the garments of salvation, saying: “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” [11]; as though the garments of salvation were the righteousness of Christ and His praise, which He gives us as a free gift from His own.

62.0.s.en: 1. A new name and a glorious life:

62.0.0.en: 1 For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. 2 And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name. 3 Thou shalt also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.

62.0.1.en: “For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all the nations thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name” [1-2].

62.0.2.en: The speaker here is the Word of God, in whose heart the Church holds the central place; for He came into the world to betroth her to Himself as an eternal bride. If Boaz did not rest until he had completed the matter of his marriage to Ruth the Gentile (Ruth 3:18), then the Lord Christ does not cease His constant work until He has joined to Himself, as His bride, the Church that He acquired with His precious blood. He is the Sun of righteousness who shines upon her, so that she bears His righteousness as her own righteousness. She enjoys splendor and becomes a spiritual lamp that all the winds of the world cannot extinguish. He speaks to her, saying: “And thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord Christ” (Ezek 16:13-14).

62.0.3.en: The Lord Christ gives her His splendor within her and His glory as glory for her, so that she enjoys the renewal that reaches even the name, the sign of complete renewal: “And thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name.” For when the Lord Christ came and by His Holy Spirit gave us renewal, we took His name as a new name and became “Christians.” For this reason the early apologists, such as the philosopher Athenagoras, said: [The true accusation that was brought against the Christians was the accusation of “the Name.” The persecution against them was fierce not because of a crime they had committed, but because of the name they bore.

62.1.0.en: The Church of the New Testament enjoyed being attributed to the name of the Savior as a living source for enjoying His surpassing righteousness as the secret of her beauty: “Thou shalt also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God” [3]. The Lord calls her a “crown of beauty” and a “royal diadem,” not that she may be placed on the head of the Lord, for He needs no additional honor, but that she is in His hand; she is the work of His hands, her glory is of His own making. He cherishes her, and He remains the Head while she is His glorious body.

62.2.0.en: 4 Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. 5 For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.

62.2.1.en: One of the new names that the Church has enjoyed is “the bride of Christ.” “Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee” [4-5].

62.2.2.en: Outside Christ the Savior she was called “Forsaken” and “Desolate,” like a barren land without life or fruit, and like a girl whom everyone has abandoned, so that she became a ruined soul crushed by the feeling of isolation and desertion. Now, in Christ, she has become an eternal heavenly bride; therefore she has taken two honored titles in place of the two former names: “Hephzibah,” which means “my delight is in her,” and “Beulah,” that is, “the one who has a husband” or “married.” She has become the object of God's delight, living in the bosom of her heavenly Bridegroom.

62.2.3.en: Her sons love her land and work with joy and gladness as though they were married to the Church, working on her behalf not as slaves nor as hired servants awaiting their reward, but as a husband who delights in his bride, seeking her rest and her comfort... This is the mark of the children of God, who with joy dedicate their hearts, their thoughts and their energies to work in the Church of Christ.

62.2.4.en: It is noted that this bride is unique and wonderful in the following respects:

62.2.5.en: a. She is a virgin and at the same time a mother who has sons, a thing that will not be realized in the life of any girl, but it was realized in the holy Virgin Mary, the Theotokos. She bore Jesus, the Lord of glory, and remained ever-virgin, because her Son is the Giver of virginity, and so she became the most perfect member of the Church.

62.2.6.en: Our Church is a chaste virgin (2 Cor 11:2), and she is at the same time the mother of the believers.

62.2.7.en: We also, when we receive membership in the Church, have our souls become chaste virgins within, and through love they bear a kind of motherhood toward human beings.

62.2.9.en: Truly, many cannot be virgins according to the flesh, but every believer is bound to be a virgin according to the spirit.

62.2.10.en: Therefore awake, O my soul, and take care of your virginity.

62.2.11.en: * The mother of the Lord Christ is a virgin, and His bride, “the Church,” is also a virgin.

62.2.12.en: St. Ambrose * Grace made the Virgin a mother and did not dissolve her virginity.

62.3.0.en: Father Theodotus, Bishop of Ancyra b. By saying: “As a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee” [5], he reveals the unity of the Church, for he regarded all her children as one young man, because all live with one aim and one goal, which is union with the Father in His Son Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit. On the other hand, he makes clear that he does not mean marriage in the bodily sense, for it is not fitting for sons to marry their mother, but he means the attachment of the children of God to His bride the Church and their union with her. Finally, the likening of the children of the Church to a young man means that they are marked by perpetual youthfulness, in which old age does not overtake them and weakness does not afflict them.

62.3.1.en: c. By saying: “And as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee” [5], he reveals that the Church is marked by perpetual joy, and that she remains in a state of perpetual wedding in which each of the two parties longs for the other. In other words, the wedding does not grow old and is not subject to time, but remains an eternal, perpetual wedding.

62.3.2.en: It is wonderful that in the rite of the Coptic Church, during the Marriage service, attention is directed toward the Church as the bride of Christ, and also toward St. Mary as a living example of enjoying an inner wedding with the Lord Christ. At the end of the service of this Liturgy the deacons chant this hymn:

62.3.3.en: “Hail to the shining bride, the mother of Him who shines; hail to her who received into herself the Word who is in her womb; hail to her who is more honorable than the Cherubim; hail to her who bore for us the Savior of our souls...”.

62.4.0.en: 6 I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, 7 and let him not keep silence, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth. 8 The LORD hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, “Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured: 9 But they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the LORD; and they that have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of my holiness.”

62.4.1.en: The Jews suffered the captivity and regarded themselves as a wife forsaken by her husband, or as a land that had become desolate; and behold, the Lord brings them back to be sons working in their land (their country). But perhaps some feared being exposed to captivity once more; therefore the Lord affirms His watching over His people who have returned to Him.

62.4.2.en: If the enemy of good took us captive in his land, and deprived us of the promised land and of the enjoyment of the heavenly holy things, now through the Cross we have become the bride of the Lord, and we have returned, as it were, to Paradise as a house of our own, or as a holy city in which we dwell with our God, who sets a strict and vigilant guard at our walls, watching the enemy night and day without ceasing [6].

62.4.3.en: Who are these watchmen whom the Lord sets over His Church but His faithful and vigilant servants, especially in the spirit of constant prayer together with pastoral work filled with love? This is what we perceive in the ministry of the Apostle Paul, who says: “Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears” (Acts 20:31). And also in the ministry of the prophet Samuel, who says: “Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way” (1 Sam 12:23). Thus constant prayer is joined with love and with continual teaching, all of them being the work of watching over the city of the Lord.

62.4.4.en: In the life of the true Christian who has practical spiritual knowledge—the Gnostic—it is necessary to set up a constant inner watch, which St. Clement of Alexandria expressed by saying: [It is fitting for the Gnostic to contemplate God as far as possible].

62.4.5.en: How wonderful is the statement: “Ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, and let him not keep silence” [6-7]. Thus the Lord calls us to remember Him continually and not to be silent, and then He too answers and is not silent; we remember Him and He remembers us, for He longs to bring us into strong and continuous dealings with Him, asking that we be established like His glorious Jerusalem, and that He make of us “a praise in the earth” [7]. Everyone who looks at us or comes into contact with us enjoys an icon of heaven, true inner joy.

62.4.6.en: God grants us to enjoy the fruit of His Holy Spirit, wheat and wine, without the enemy seizing it from us. What is the wheat but the enjoyment of fellowship with Christ, the unique ear of grain?! And what is the wine but the gift of the Holy Spirit, the Giver of joy?! It is as though our watchfulness in the Lord preserves our fellowship with God in Jesus Christ, our heavenly wheat, by means of His Holy Spirit, the unique wine.

62.5.0.en: 10 Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people. 11 Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, “Behold, thy Saviour cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.” 12 And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.

62.5.1.en: Preparing the way for the Lord in our life is a preparing of our own way into His heavens. He passes through to the gates of our hearts to carry us to His everlasting gates. He set up His Cross as a banner of love for us, that by it we may pass through the spiritual battle and receive the heavenly reward. Therefore it was said: “Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people. Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world; say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy Saviour cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him” [10-11].

62.5.2.en: St. John the Baptist came to prepare the way for the Lord (Mt 3:3), but the One who truly works and who rewards is the Savior of the Church.
